A quality-of-life release, inspired by a feature comparison with Zipline. It takes what fits featherdrop's zero-knowledge, no-accounts approach and hardens the rest. Just update the container, `/data` and `/config` stay untouched.

## ✨ Added

- Paste to upload: Ctrl/Cmd+V anywhere on the page drops the files on your clipboard (a screenshot, for example) straight into the selection. Pasting into text fields works as usual.
- Remembered options: your last expiry, download limit and metadata choice come back on your next visit. They are stored locally in your browser, and the password never is.
- Photo metadata removal: JPEGs can be stripped of EXIF, GPS and IPTC data in the browser, before encryption. The server never sees plaintext, so the browser is the only place this can happen. It's on by default when you select a JPEG, and one switch keeps the metadata. A photo that can't be parsed is uploaded untouched instead of being risked.
- Install it as an app (PWA): featherdrop is installable and registers as an Android share target, so "Share → featherdrop" from any app drops the shared files into the normal upload flow.
- Operator guardrails, all optional: `MAX_EXPIRY` caps the longest expiry (the UI hides longer options and the server rejects them). `STORAGE_QUOTA` caps the total bytes and rejects an over-quota upload with HTTP 507 before a single byte lands. `RATE_LIMIT` puts per-IP token buckets on upload, finalize, download and password attempts, is on by default, and answers with 429 and `Retry-After`. `TRUST_PROXY` keys the limits on `X-Forwarded-For` behind a reverse proxy. With these in place, running an instance that's reachable from the internet is a reasonable thing to do.
- Container healthcheck: `GET /api/healthcheck` and a Dockerfile `HEALTHCHECK` (a self-check flag that works in the distroless image), so Docker and Unraid show a real health state.

## 🎨 Design

- A shorter README with new pictures. It opens with download buttons, shows the upload options, the finished link and the recipient's page on three new screenshots, and keeps the setup to what a first start needs.

## ⚡ Improved

- Share pages opt out of search engines: `robots.txt`, plus `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` on every share and download response. The header is the same on 200, 401 and 404, so it doesn't reveal whether a share exists.
- Config is checked at boot: an invalid value for one of the new variables stops the start with a clear message naming the variable. A `BASE_URL` that isn't absolute and a short `UPLOAD_PASSWORD` log a warning.
- An audit of the delete, finalize and download paths, prompted by the recent CVE round in a comparable project, found no gaps. Every token comparison is constant-time, 404s look the same, and there's no route that changes anything without authentication. The new rate limiter also throttles guesses against the key verifier.

## 🐛 Fixed

- The operator's `DEFAULT_EXPIRY` is used as the starting expiry again. The app had been ignoring it.
